name: Parent PID Spoofing with BlockDLLs
command: CreateProcess with PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS set to a chosen PID
description: Parent PID (PPID) spoofing uses UpdateProcThreadAttribute with PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS to make a new process appear to be a child of an attacker-chosen parent (for example explorer.exe), defeating parent-child heuristics that flag, say, Word spawning PowerShell. It is usually paired with the BlockDLLs attribute (PROCESS_CREATION_MITIGATION_POLICY_BLOCK_NON_MICROSOFT_BINARIES) to stop non-Microsoft (EDR hook) DLLs loading into the child.
source: MITRE ATT&CK T1134.004; public PPID-spoofing and BlockDLLs research
notes:
=== MECHANISM (Win32) ===
  InitializeProcThreadAttributeList
  UpdateProcThreadAttribute(..., PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS, &hParent, ...)
  # child's PPID in the kernel points at hParent; the child also inherits that parent's token.
  CreateProcess(..., EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT, &si.StartupInfo, &pi)

=== BLOCKDLLS (pair with it) ===
  UpdateProcThreadAttribute(..., PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_MITIGATION_POLICY,
     PROCESS_CREATION_MITIGATION_POLICY_BLOCK_NON_MICROSOFT_BINARIES_ALWAYS_ON ...)
  # prevents non-Microsoft-signed DLLs (many EDR user-mode hooks) from loading into the child.

=== WHY IT EVADES ===
  - Breaks "Office spawned a shell" and similar parent-child detections.
  - Child inherits the spoofed parent's security token (handle must have PROCESS_CREATE_PROCESS).
  - BlockDLLs strips the EDR's in-process visibility.

=== TELLS ===
  - PPID points at a parent that did not actually call CreateProcess (ETW process-start parent vs
    kernel callback parent mismatch).
  - Built into Cobalt Strike (ppid / blockdlls), available in many loaders.

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Process hollowing (identity via image), direct token theft, scheduled-task spawning.

examples.label: Enumerate parent-child relationships to baseline (defender view)

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1134.004 - Parent PID Spoofing

recommended.note: Hollowing fakes the image; PPID spoofing fakes the parent - often combined.
PPID spoofing commonly precedes injecting into the spoofed child.
Where parent-child spoofing fits in evasion.

defense.why_it_works: The ProcessParameters parent handle supplied through PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PARENT_PROCESS sets the PPID recorded in the process object, and the child inherits that parent's token. Detections that trust the recorded PPID (e.g. flagging Office spawning a shell) are blinded, and BlockDLLs removes the EDR's user-mode hooks from the new process.
defense.prerequisites: Code execution and a handle to the chosen parent with PROCESS_CREATE_PROCESS rights. Spoofing a higher-integrity parent still requires rights to that process (often admin/SYSTEM).
defense.impact: T1134.004 Access Token Manipulation: Parent PID Spoofing. Breaks parent-child detection logic, can inherit a more trusted token, and (with BlockDLLs) strips EDR user-mode visibility from the child.
defense.detection: Correlate the kernel process-creation callback parent (authoritative, via EDR/ETW Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Process) against the recorded PPID; a mismatch is high-fidelity. Also alert on the BlockDLLs mitigation policy being set on a non-Microsoft-launched process, and on blocked non-Microsoft DLL load events (code-integrity 3033).
defense.artifacts: ETW Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Process process-start vs Sysmon EID 1 ParentImage mismatch; CodeIntegrity 3033 (image did not meet signing requirement for the BlockDLLs process); Sysmon EID 1 showing a child of explorer.exe that explorer never created.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1
| eval kernel_parent=ParentProcessGuid
| join type=left ProcessGuid [search index=etw sourcetype="Kernel-Process" | fields ProcessGuid, RealParentImage]
| where isnotnull(RealParentImage) AND RealParentImage!=ParentImage
| table _time, Computer, Image, ParentImage, RealParentImage
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("userinit.exe","winlogon.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
defense.prevention: Rely on EDR that reports the authoritative kernel parent rather than the recorded PPID; enable Protected Process Light for EDR so BlockDLLs cannot strip a kernel sensor; apply ASR and WDAC so the spoofed child still cannot load unsigned code; restrict handle rights to sensitive parents (explorer, lsass) via least privilege.

detections.name: Recorded parent does not match kernel launcher
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","svchost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("userinit.exe","winlogon.exe","services.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
detections.false_positives: Shell restarts and some login flows
detections.tuning: Baseline legitimate explorer/svchost parents per environment

detections.name: BlockDLLs - non-Microsoft image load blocked (CodeIntegrity 3033)
detections.logic:
index=wineventlog source="*CodeIntegrity*" EventCode=3033
| table _time, Computer, ProcessName, FileNameBuffer
detections.false_positives: Rare; some legitimate software sets binary signature policy
detections.tuning: Allowlist known hardened applications that enable BlockDLLs themselves
